# Start a new paper

Each paper is a fresh clone of this template. You keep the structure; you swap in your data, variables, and narrative.

## 1. Create the repo from the template

Use the GitHub **"Use this template"** button, or the CLI:

```bash
gh repo create my-new-paper --template connectors-testing-pplx/research-paper-template --public --clone
cd my-new-paper
```

If you cloned instead of templating, just `git remote set-url origin <your-new-repo>`.

## 2. Rename the project

Open `_quarto.yml` and `paper/_quarto.yml` and change `title:` to your paper's working title. Update the `repo-url` in the root `_quarto.yml` to point at your new repo.

## 3. Restore the library and add your data

```r
renv::restore()
```

Drop your raw files into `data/raw/`. Keep them untouched — the pipeline writes derivatives to `data/processed/`.

## 4. Edit the config

`analysis/00-config.R` is the single place to define file paths, variable names, and grouping variables. Most papers only edit this file and the manuscript.

## 5. Run the pipeline

```bash
Rscript analysis/run-all.R
```

This executes `01-import` → `06-report` in order, writing figures and tables to `outputs/` and a processed dataset to `data/processed/`.

## 6. Write and render the manuscript

Edit `paper/paper.qmd`. Pull in pipeline outputs with `knitr::include_graphics()` and `gt::gt()` chunks. Render:

```bash
quarto render paper/paper.qmd --to pdf
quarto render paper/paper.qmd --to docx
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Repo created from template
- [ ] `renv::restore()` ran cleanly
- [ ] Raw data in `data/raw/`
- [ ] `analysis/00-config.R` updated with variable names
- [ ] `run-all.R` completes without error
- [ ] Manuscript renders to PDF and Word
- [ ] `renv::snapshot()` committed with new packages
